newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai mills seek new end-Sept corn import deadline.
newsitem.headline: Thai mills seek new end-Sept corn import deadline.

text.p: Thailand's corn market was quiet this week as the excitement following the approval of 150,000 tonnes in duty-free corn imports evaporated after feedmills found they could not get cargoes within the quota deadline.
The feed industry is now asking the government to extend the deadline for the duty-free imports to end-September instead of end-August, trade sources said.

On July 29, the Thai government announced it would allow the industry to import 150,000 tonnes of corn without tariffs to alleviate short-term shortages caused by drought, but on condition the imports were delivered by August 31.
"At first, we thought we could buy cargoes in transit to meet the deadline. But after checking we found that we couldn't get a single one," a Singapore-based trader said.
"If anyone would like to buy from me now, I can get cargoes from Pacific Northwest but it will be tough for me to have them delivered by August 31," he said.
Normally, Thai buyers could buy cargoes in transit for Japan, Indonesia, and Malaysia, at short notice.
"Demand in those countries is quite strong at the moment. To divert any cargo from Indonesia, for example, would be difficult," said a trader in Bangkok.
"And if we do, we have to pay high premiums and that makes it unattractive. That's why we have tonnes of inquries after the approval but no actual orders," he said.
So far, only a few poultry growers had imported the corn, and at least 50,000-75,000 tonnes remained to be covered, according to market sources.
Meanwhile the local corn prices rose further to 5.30-5.40 baht a kg this week from 5.20 baht a kg last week.
"Feed producers have now turned to broken rice as a subtitute for corn. We hope the government will extend the deadline for imports," said a supply manager from a major local feed producer.
Oilseed and meal trade in the C&F market was lacklustre with only small purchases of rapeseed and sunflower meal from India, reported, traders said.
More supplies of soymeal were expected later this week and into next week, trade sources said.
The vessel Solidanoft was scheduled to arrive this Sunday with 55,000 tonnes of Argentine soymeal and soybeans. Chareon Pokphand was said to be the buyer, traders said.
Another ship, Toscana, was expected to arrive with 39,000 tonnes of Argentine soymeal and sunflower meal.
Local soymeal price was steady at 10.00 baht a kg, unchanged from last week.
